messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In lions, the most striking example of a dominant genetic trait is the **presence of a mane** in adult males. The gene(s) that control mane development are expressed whenever at least one copy is present, so a single dominant allele is enough to produce the full mane phenotype. This is why all male lions have manes (though the size and darkness vary), whereas females lack them entirely.
